unresolved_items: The assigned passages are recitals of Regulation (EU) 2026/1744. Their operative legal effect and current application must be checked against the amended Articles 30, 43 and 75 before any obligation or prohibition is published.
The EDPB list is expressly non-prescriptive and non-exhaustive; it does not by itself establish anonymity, compliance or a universal testing threshold.
OWASP guidance describes threats and control expectations; it does not certify a particular open-weight artifact or establish a universal legal requirement.
CoSAI is a non-binding framework. Table-derived mitigation wording on Pages 15 and 19 should not be treated as a complete control specification without visual or contextual review.

evidence_candidates.claim: The recital describes a conformity-assessment route for a high-risk AI system covered by Union harmonisation legislation and explains how quality-management-system aspects under the AI Act may be included within the corresponding harmonisation-law quality-management system; it also describes transitional assessment powers for certain notified bodies.
qualifiers: This is recital context and does not replace the operative amended provision.
The transitional period and conditions must be checked against the operative text and current dates.

evidence_candidates.claim: The recital states that the Commission is responsible for pre-market conformity assessments for AI systems under the AI Office's exclusive supervision when those systems are subject to third-party conformity assessment.
qualifiers: The statement is limited to the supervision and assessment conditions described in the recital.
uncertainties: Confirm the operative allocation of responsibility and the system categories currently in scope.

evidence_candidates.claim: The recital states that conformity-assessment bodies designated under the Regulation may conduct assessments only for the relevant categories and types of high-risk AI systems, with codes used to specify the designation scope.
qualifiers: The recital describes the designation scope; the operative Article 30 and Article 43 text must control publication.

evidence_candidates.claim: The EDPB describes a non-prescriptive and non-exhaustive set of elements that supervisory authorities may consider when assessing a controller's claim of model anonymity; deployment context and the likely means available to other persons can affect the level and nature of testing considered.
qualifiers: The source says that alternative approaches may be possible when they provide equivalent protection.

evidence_candidates.claim: The EDPB assessment elements include source selection, data preparation and minimisation, methodological choices such as privacy-preserving techniques, and measures applied to model outputs.
qualifiers: Differential privacy is given as an example; the list does not establish that one technique is sufficient.

evidence_candidates.claim: The EDPB describes document-based audits, code-review reports and theoretical analysis as material that may be considered when assessing whether model-design measures reduce the likelihood of re-identification.

The EDPB says testing scope, frequency, quantity and quality should be considered and gives attribute or membership inference, exfiltration, training-data regurgitation, model inversion and reconstruction as examples of attacks for structured testing; it also identifies DPIA, DPO, lifecycle and threat-model documentation as relevant to an anonymity claim.
qualifiers: Successful testing is evidence only for the attacks actually covered.

evidence_candidates.claim: OWASP describes weak provenance and unsigned or mutable model artifacts as supply-chain risks: model cards do not prove origin, and artifacts resolved by mutable references without signatures or hash pins can be replaced or altered at transit, storage or promotion boundaries.

OWASP identifies adapter application, model conversion, merging and quantisation as transformation risks because malicious changes may be introduced and assurances for a full-precision or source artifact may not transfer to the deployed artifact.
OWASP describes extraction, membership inference and inversion against open-weight deployments as offline attacks with unbounded rates, making the access mode itself part of the attack surface.
qualifiers: This is a threat description, not a finding that every open-weight model is vulnerable.

evidence_candidates.claim: CoSAI identifies precise version identifiers, origins, checksums or content hashes, usage statistics and preprocessing transformations as model and training-data provenance elements, and describes signed artifacts, secure storage, integrity verification, access controls and tamper-evident logging for checkpoints.
qualifiers: The source is a framework and its controls are recommendations, not universal obligations.

evidence_candidates.claim: CoSAI identifies code protection, pre-trained-model and checkpoint integrity, access controls, cryptographic signatures and tamper-proof evaluation documentation as controls addressing architecture backdoors, weight tampering and compromised evaluation.
qualifiers: The threat-summary table is transcribed in the validated unit; table layout and completeness were not independently established here.

evidence_candidates.claim: CoSAI identifies checkpoint, training-job and model-conversion supply-chain risks and describes infrastructure attestations, dependency-scanning reports, secure access logs, end-to-end model provenance and independent third-party assessments as assurance evidence.
qualifiers: The source is non-binding and the threat-summary table may require visual review for complete row context.

evidence_candidates.claim: CoSAI recommends cryptographic verification and provenance verification for model artifacts and training data, lifecycle integrity monitoring, model-tampering incident playbooks and least-privilege controls; it also describes data-security and model-integrity review for third-party AI applications.
qualifiers: These are framework recommendations and require deployment-specific risk assessment.

classification_proposals.basis: Reviewed Regulation (EU) 2026/1744; assigned passages are recitals and require operative-text qualification.
EDPB Opinion 28/2024 provides supervisory guidance and expressly describes the assessment list as non-prescriptive.
OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications is security guidance describing risks and control expectations.
CoSAI Establish Risks and Controls for the AI Supply Chain is a non-binding framework.

unresolved_items: Resolve the operative legal provisions, designation scope and temporal applicability behind the SRC-0043 recitals before binding publication.
Confirm whether visual review is required for the table-dependent SRC-0034 candidates before using detailed mitigation mappings.
Do not infer that open-weight availability, a signature, a privacy technique or a framework control establishes safety, anonymity, licensing or regulatory compliance.
